newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Straddles traded in Abbey National.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Straddles traded in Abbey National.

text.p: Large deals in the UK equity options market were few and far between by early afternoon on Monday, dealers said.
"It's been fairly quiet so far and people are waiting for this week's economic and corporate data to come out before making their next move (in options)," said one dealer.
In stock options banking group Abbey National was singled out for a flurry of mixed trades as traders with different opinions of the underlying shares either bought or sold medium-term straddles.
By 1400 GMT, a total of 850 puts and calls had been traded in the July 750 series.
The main purchaser -- who expects the underlying shares to be volatile -- bought the options at 86-1/2p and the main seller -- expecting volatility to be flat or decrease -- sold them at 85p.
Abbey National shares fell 7p to 748-1/2p as Lehman Brothers repeated their cautious stance on the stock.
A long straddle was the main deal in aero-engine manufacturer Rolls Royce in which 250 May 240 puts were bought at 17p along with 250 May 240 calls at 13p.
The underlying shares added 1-1/2p to 234-1/2p and for the straddle to show a profit at expiry, Rolls Royce shares need to either fall below 210p or go above 270p.
Elsewhere, in the FTSE futures market the bulk of deals was from traders rolling forward positions ahead of March expiry.

Of the 3,600 lots traded in the March contract by the afternoon, around 1,100 were rolled forward into June futures with a spread -- or difference in price between the June and March contracts -- of about 20-1/2p.
By 1400 GMT, March FTSE futures were down two points at 4283 while June futures were up 1.5 at 4306. The cash FTSE 100 index had shed 7.7 points to 4300.6.
